Clinical Treatment Summary
The patient presented for evaluation of neck pain and stiffness following a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Symptoms began
shortly after the event and are consistent in location and character with the mechanism of injury described. Two office visits were
completed. On examination, there was reduced range of motion of the cervical spine and tenderness over the paraspinal muscles,
findings that support a soft tissue strain. Neurological screening, including reflexes, strength, and sensation in both upper
extremities, was within normal limits. The patient reports a remote history of a minor strain in the same region, which reoslved
completely with no lasting limitation. Treatment consisted of conservative care, including home stretching, activity modification,
and as-needed anti-inflammatory medication, and followed the expected course for this type of injury. Symptoms improved
steadily, and no further follow-up was needed at the time of discharge from care. Billing records reflect single charges for each
visit with no duplicate entries.
